item.title: PiGuard v3.6.8 (build 718)
item.description:
What's new

  • Fix: Desktop widget now shows live data instead of stale cached statistics. The app group was renamed to the team-prefixed form (GB7Z2TZ8LT.com.foosmith.PiGuard) — the iOS-style group. prefix requires provisioning-profile authorization on macOS 15+, which blocked the sandboxed widget from reading the snapshot file the app publishes. The widget now reads fresh data directly on every refresh.
  • Fix: Widget timestamp ticks in real time. The "X min ago" label now updates continuously on screen instead of freezing at the last render.
  • Fix: "App not running · cached" warning is now reliable. The warning is pre-scheduled into the widget timeline, so it appears on time even when macOS throttles widget refreshes — and no longer shows while data is actually fresh.
  • Removed the defunct keychain snapshot channel.
  • Widget timeline reloads at least every 15 minutes to avoid a stale display (carried over from the unreleased 3.6.8 bump).
  • Widget tap opens the Query Log via AppDelegate wiring (carried over from the unreleased 3.6.8 bump).

Requirements

macOS 13 or later.

Note: this build is Developer ID-signed but not notarized — on first launch use right-click → Open if Gatekeeper objects.

item.title: PiGuard v3.6.8 (build 718)
item.description:
What's new

  • Fix: Tapping the desktop widget now actually opens the Query Log. The previous release's widgetURL deep link never ran because the app's AppDelegate was not connected as the application delegate (the delegate outlet in MainMenu.xib was attached to the menu instead of File's Owner), so the piguard:// URL was never handled. The delegate is now wired correctly.
  • Fix: Clearer Local Network permission prompt. Added NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription so macOS explains why PiGuard needs local network access to reach your Pi-hole servers. (If your servers show offline after updating, enable PiGuard under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network.)
  • Fix: Widget no longer gets stuck on a stale status. The widget timeline now refreshes at least every 15 minutes, so it recovers promptly after the Pi-holes go from offline back to online even without a status change.

Requirements

macOS 13 or later.

item.title: PiGuard v3.6.7 (build 717)
item.description:
What's new

  • Fix: Desktop widget now opens the Query Log when clicked. Replaced the AppIntent-based tap handler with a widgetURL deep link (piguard://open-query-log), which is reliably handled by macOS on macOS 26 for LSUIElement apps. The previous approach using Button(intent:) with openAppWhenRun = true was not consistently routing the intent to the main app process or activating the window.

Requirements

macOS 13 or later.

item.title: PiGuard v3.6.6 (build 716)
item.description:
Bug Fixes

  • Auto-update repaired — the Sparkle appcast pipeline had been failing silently, so apps on 3.6.1–3.6.4 were never offered updates. The feed is fixed and updates flow again.
  • Update loop fixed — the app's build number (CFBundleVersion) was stuck at 713 regardless of the released build, which could cause Sparkle to re-offer the same update repeatedly.

Security Hardening

  • Pi-hole API token is now percent-encoded in request URLs, so tokens containing reserved characters (&, =, +, #, ?) can no longer break or alter the request
  • Debug log file is now restricted to owner-only permissions (it can contain DNS query history)
  • Release-notes rendering in the update feed hardened against XML/CDATA injection

Install

  1. Download PiGuard-3.6.6-716-macOS.dmg
  2. Open the DMG and drag PiGuard into Applications
  3. Launch from Launchpad or Applications

item.title: PiGuard v3.6.5 (build 715)
item.description:
What's New

  • Preferences — per-server enable/disable toggle in the server list; disabled servers are excluded from polling and control actions
  • Shortcuts removed — keyboard shortcut feature (⌘⌥⇧P) and all menu key equivalents removed

Install

  1. Download PiGuard-3.6.5-macOS.dmg
  2. Open the DMG and drag PiGuard into Applications
  3. Launch from Launchpad or Applications

Requires macOS 13 or later. Signed with a Developer ID certificate.
